answer.rationale:
The competitor price cut creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, and memory_73 endorses it in exactly those terms. But the recovered source exp_73 shows the consolidation dropped the decisive fact: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% came with 30-day retention -12%, i.e. the acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, and the source explicitly warns against generalizing discounting as sustainable growth. Against the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue), promotional pricing is disqualified — it would buy this week's churn numbers by importing a cohort that churns next quarter, and would also deepen a price war on the competitor's chosen ground. I treat memory_73 as a known-lossy summary and do not act on it.

Of the remaining options, only the signup/onboarding line has a recovered source: exp_31 confirms signup simplification on SMB with signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, and retention essentially flat at -1% — the profile of a genuine, durable lift rather than a borrowed one. It also targets the segment actually under attack, and improves the non-price value proposition (faster time-to-value), which is the right competitive counter to a discount. Caveat preserved: exp_31 is confirmed only on SMB and was not replicated elsewhere, and memory_86 (shortening onboarding more broadly) is an unverified consolidation that may carry the same kind of omitted downside as memory_73 — so I lean on memory_31's verified evidence and use memory_86 only as directional support, scoping the effort to SMB.

Scale: standard_experiment, restricted to SMB self-serve, with 30-day retention as an explicit guardrail metric rather than only activation/signup — the failure mode revealed by exp_73 is precisely a metric that looks good early and rots at renewal. Not a broad rollout, because the evidence base is one segment and several inherited memories are unverified. referral_incentive (memory_57), activation_messaging (memory_91) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) remain plausible but rest on unverified consolidations of the same style that misled on memory_73; they are queued for verification next cycle, not acted on today. If leadership needs an immediate price-facing gesture, it should be time-boxed and separately measured on renewal survival, not adopted as strategy.
